# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 5 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 5
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. For to this end the Lord endured to deliver his flesh to corruption, so that we might be sanctified through the forgiveness of sins — that is, through his sprinkled blood.
2. For the scripture about him has things in part concerning Israel, and in part things concerning us; and it says thus: "He was wounded because of our sins and was afflicted because of our iniquities; by his wound we were healed. As a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and as a lamb silent before its shearer."
3. We ought therefore to give great thanks to the Lord, because he revealed to us things past and gave us wisdom concerning the present things and we are not without understanding concerning the things to come.
4. But the scripture says: "Not unjustly spread nets for birds." This means that a man who has knowledge of the way of righteousness but steers himself away into the way of darkness — he will justly perish.
5. There is yet this, brothers: if the Lord endured to suffer for our soul, though he was Lord of the whole world, to whom God said at the foundation of the world, "Let us make the human being according to our image and likeness," how then did he endure to suffer at the hands of human beings?
6. Learn! The prophets, having received grace from him, prophesied about him. But he himself — in order to destroy death and to demonstrate the resurrection of the dead — endured to be manifested in flesh, so that he might pay back to our fathers the debt of the promise and, while preparing a new people for himself, might show while he was on earth that after the resurrection he himself will judge.
7. Furthermore, while teaching Israel and doing such great signs and wonders, he preached to them and loved them exceedingly.
8. But when he chose his own apostles who were to preach his gospel, they were beyond all sin, in order that he might show that he came not to call the righteous but sinners — then he manifested himself as the Son of God.
9. For if he had not come in the flesh, how could people have been saved by looking at him? — since, looking at the sun which is the work of his hands and will cease to be, they are not able to gaze into its beams.
10. Therefore the Son of God came in flesh for this reason: that he might bring the total of the sins of those who persecuted his prophets unto death.
11. To this end therefore he endured. For God says the chastening of his flesh is from them: "Strike the shepherd and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered."
12. And he himself willed to suffer thus, because it was necessary that he suffer on a tree; for the prophet says about him: "Spare my soul from the sword" and "Pierce my flesh with nails, because companies of evildoers have risen up against me."
13. And again he says: "Behold, I have given my back to stripes, and my cheeks to blows, and my face I set as a hard rock."
